subject: chemistry

moments.title: Thomson's parabolas
moments.body: Thomson, examining canal rays, finds neon gives two parabolas — masses 20 and 22. The first evidence of stable isotopes.
moments.takeaway: Stable isotopes are discovered. The atom of an element has variants.

moments.title: Aston's mass spectrograph
moments.body: Aston refines Thomson's instrument and discovers 212 of the 287 naturally occurring isotopes. He wins the 1922 Nobel.
moments.takeaway: Most of the periodic table has multiple isotopes.

moments.title: Soft ionisation
moments.body: MALDI and electrospray let mass spec analyse intact proteins and DNA without fragmenting them. Tanaka and Fenn share the 2002 Nobel.
moments.takeaway: Mass spectrometry can now weigh biomolecules.

moments.title: Proteomics and metabolomics
moments.body: High-resolution mass spec routinely identifies thousands of proteins from a single sample. COVID-19 vaccines were characterised by mass spec.
moments.takeaway: Mass spec is now the workhorse of pharmaceutical and clinical chemistry.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Modern Orbitrap and FT-ICR mass spectrometers reach resolving power > 10^6. Single-cell proteomics is emerging. Forensic mass spec identifies drugs at sub-nanogram levels.
now.open_questions: Can single-molecule mass spec become quantitative? Can MS image proteins in tissue at high resolution?

reflection: Aston discovered 212 isotopes by hand. Modern instruments find them in seconds. Has automation changed what 'discovery' means?
